newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar reflects on one year in power.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar reflects on one year in power.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, reflecting on his first year in power, was quoted on Sunday as saying his proudest achievements so far were a political pact reached with the nationalists and deals on pensions and labour reforms.

In an interview with the daily newspaper El Mundo, Aznar also said he was delighted by the economic progress made during the year which brought Spain closer to making the first wave of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union in 1999.

Asked what were his happiest days in power, he replied: "The day that we reached an accord with the nationalists that no one thought possible. They day we signed an agreement on pensions that calmed a large sector of our society; and the day that employers and unions reached a deal on labour reform."

The PP ended 13 years of Socialist rule in Spain when they emerged from a general election last year as the biggest party in parliament. But they emerged 20 seats short of an absolute majority and had to secure the backing of smaller nationalist parties to form a government.
While Aznar trumpeted his government's economic accomplishments, he said he was still anxious about the level of unemployment in Spain.
"During 1996, unemployment fell by 178,000 people, but this continues to be a big problem. That is why the accord between employers and unions is so important," he said.
The PP, which formed the centre-right government on May 5, 1996, has delivered dramatic declines in interest rates, inflation and public expenditure that have won the respect of friend and foe alike.

But Spain's unemployment rate remains among the highest in Europe at just under 22 percent. The government hopes that a deal between unions and employers on labour reforms will go some way toward reducing that towering level of joblessness.
In another deal with unions, the government signed an accord in October last year to guarantee the buying power and future payment of pensions.
